ops.title: A consumer that resolves its app path from $HOME splits from daemonkit's passwd-derived agent paths
ops.body:
A consumer-integration hazard found 2026-08-29 while migrating the fleet to daemonkit v0.23.0. It is daemonkit-side context for a defect that manifests in a consumer; the consumer half is filed in captain-hook's own records.

## The invariant

daemonkit resolves the user's home through the **passwd database**, not `$HOME` — deliberately, so a sandboxed or remapped environment cannot relocate state (`paths/paths.go`, `internal/realhome`). The one sanctioned override is `DAEMONKIT_HOME`. Every path daemonkit owns follows from that: agent plists (`launchd/agent.go:156`), per-daemon state (`paths.Agent(label)`), the staged program dir (`~/.daemonkit/bin/<label>`), the artifact cache.

## The hazard

A consumer that derives its **own** installed-application path from `os.UserHomeDir()` — i.e. `$HOME` — while daemonkit derives the **agent and state** paths from passwd has made those two halves independently resolvable. Under any caller with a remapped `HOME` they converge *different machines*: the app lands in one home, the LaunchAgent and state in another. Neither half is wrong on its own terms, and nothing in either path reports a conflict.

captain-hook hit exactly this. `internal/hookd/deployment.go:56-64` resolves the app root from `os.UserHomeDir()`, guarded only by a canonicality check:

```go
resolved, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(home)
if err != nil || resolved != home {
    return "", errors.New("captain package: user home must be a canonical real directory")
}
```

Homebrew remaps `HOME` to a throwaway temp dir for `post_install`. That guard used to catch it **by accident**, because the temp home came from the ambient `TMPDIR` (`/var/folders/…`, non-canonical since `/var` → `/private/var`), so `resolved != home` tripped and the deploy failed loudly. Homebrew commit `f8fcbd88e0` (2026-08-07) moved that temp home under `HOMEBREW_TEMP=/private/tmp`, which **is** canonical — the guard stopped firing, and the failure went from loud to silent. `deploy.Install`/`Supersede` returned no error while the real bundle was never touched: its inode still matched the receipt in a two-week-old `activation.json`.

The causal link to that Homebrew commit is inference forced by the evidence rather than direct observation, but the split itself is directly observed.

## Why it is worth a daemonkit note rather than only a consumer bug

The `deploy` package promises **sealed** installation, activation and supersession of one fixed signed application. That seal is only as strong as the agreement between where `deploy` believes the application lives and where `launchd`/`paths` put everything else. Today a consumer supplies the former and daemonkit derives the latter, so the two can silently disagree and `Supersede` will happily seal a bundle in a throwaway directory and report success.

A canonicality check on `$HOME` is not a fix; it is a coincidence that happened to hold until an unrelated upstream change removed it.

## The shape of a real fix

Resolve the application root from the same passwd-derived source the agents use, so the app path and the agent path are not independently derivable — ideally by having `deploy` derive it rather than accept it, or by validating a caller-supplied root against `realhome` and refusing a mismatch outright. Refusing loudly is in keeping with the module's stated posture: fail fast, fail loud, no guards against impossible states — but this state *is* reachable, so it earns a real check rather than an accidental one.

Worth checking whether any other consumer derives an install root from `$HOME`; the fleet's other signed-app deployments are cc-pool's `CCPoolStatus.app` and cc-notes' helper.

Related: [[a-daemonkit-consumer-migrates-when-it-ships-not-when-its-main-is-bumped]], and the observation that a stale **staged** binary at `~/.daemonkit/bin/<label>` is re-staged only when a command that genuinely needs the daemon runs — a status or query command will not converge it.
